name: Ishmael
overview: Ishmael, a male from the tribe of Benjamin, is identified uniquely as the son of Azel according to 1 Chronicles 8:38. Beyond this genealogical note, Scripture does not provide extensive details about his life or role. His mention situates him within the broader family lines documented in the Old Testament.
namesAndTitles: The name Ishmael means 'G-d [El] he heard,' reflecting a divine response or attention, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 8:38. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries significant theological meaning rooted in Hebrew understanding.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ishmael as the son of Azel in 1 Chronicles 8:38. Other familial relationships are not detailed for this individual in the provided text, so no further family connections are documented beyond this paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: This Ishmael should not be confused with the more widely known Ishmael, son of Abraham. His mention in the genealogical record of the tribe of Benjamin underscores the preservation of family lines important to God's unfolding plan. The meaning of his name and his lineage contribute to understanding the continuity of God's people as recorded in Scripture.
